chapters.1.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches that Jesus Christ is the author of eternal salvation. Why does the Son's place give weight to the message received?
chapters.1.summary: The writer says God spoke long ago through the prophets and now through a Son. The Son is heir of all things, and through him God made the worlds. He is the radiance of God’s glory and upholds all things. After making purification for sins he sat down at God’s right hand. He is as much greater than the angels as his name is greater. The writer quotes a chain of Scriptures to show it. God calls him Son, and the angels are told to worship him. Angels are serving spirits sent to help those who will inherit salvation.
chapters.2.lds: The selected Church lesson connects Christ's suffering with his ability to help us. How does shared suffering explain the high priest's ability to help?
chapters.2.summary: The writer warns the readers not to drift from what they heard. The message spoken through angels was binding, and this salvation is greater. God did not put the coming world under angels. The writer quotes a psalm about man, made a little lower than the angels. Jesus was made lower for a time and is crowned because he died. He tasted death for everyone and calls those he saves his brothers. He shared flesh and blood to destroy the one who held death’s power. He became a merciful and faithful high priest.
chapters.3.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches responsive hearts rather than refusal of God's blessings. Why does the repeated word today require mutual encouragement?
chapters.3.summary: The writer calls Jesus the apostle and high priest of their confession. Moses was faithful in God’s house as a servant. Christ is faithful over the house as a Son, and believers are that house. The writer quotes a psalm that warns against hard hearts “today.” The fathers tested God in the wilderness for forty years. God swore they would not enter his rest. The readers must encourage one another daily. Those who left Egypt could not enter because of unbelief.
chapters.4.lds: The selected Church lesson connects Christ's suffering with offered mercy and help. How does offered mercy stand beside the exposure of hidden intentions?
chapters.4.summary: The writer says a promise of entering God’s rest still stands. The wilderness generation heard good news but did not join it with faith. God rested on the seventh day, and the psalm still says “today.” If Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken of another day. So a Sabbath rest remains for God’s people. God’s word is living and sharper than a two-edged sword. Nothing is hidden from him. Jesus the high priest was tempted in every way, yet without sin.
chapters.5.lds: The selected Church lesson applies called priestly service to authorized Church callings. Why does mature judgment require practice rather than passive hearing?
chapters.5.summary: Every high priest is chosen from among men to offer gifts and sacrifices. He can deal gently with the ignorant because he is weak himself. No one takes this honor; God calls him, as he called Aaron. Christ also did not glorify himself. God named him a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek. In his days of flesh he prayed with loud cries and tears. He learned obedience through what he suffered. The writer says the readers are slow to hear and still need milk.
chapters.6.lds: How does remembered service keep the warning connected with confident hope?
chapters.6.summary: The writer urges the readers to go on to maturity. He warns that those who fall away after enlightenment cannot be renewed. Land that drinks rain and bears thorns is burned. Yet he is persuaded of better things for these readers. God will not forget their work and their love in serving the saints. They should imitate those who inherit the promises through faith and patience. God swore to Abraham by himself. That oath gives strong encouragement and a hope like an anchor.
chapters.7.lds: The selected Church lesson connects Melchizedek Priesthood ordinances with approaching Jesus Christ. Why does continuing life answer the limit imposed by the deaths of priests?
chapters.7.summary: Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham, blessed him, and received a tenth from him. Scripture gives him no father, mother, or end of days. The writer argues that he is greater than Abraham and so than Levi. If the Levitical priesthood had brought perfection, no other priest would be needed. Jesus came from Judah and is priest by the power of an endless life. God swore that he is a priest forever. The former priests died, but he holds his priesthood permanently.
chapters.8.lds: The selected Church lesson reads ancient ordinances as pointing toward Jesus Christ. Why does the new covenant promise turn from buildings toward law within people?
chapters.8.summary: The writer gives the main point: we have a high priest seated in heaven. He serves in the true tabernacle, which the Lord set up. Priests on earth serve a copy and shadow of heavenly things. Moses was told to make everything by the pattern shown on the mountain. Jesus is mediator of a better covenant with better promises. The writer quotes Jeremiah on a new covenant with Israel and Judah. God will write his laws on hearts and remember sins no more. By saying “new,” God has made the first covenant old.
chapters.9.lds: The selected Church lesson reads ancient ordinances as pointing toward Jesus Christ. How does cleansing the conscience extend the argument beyond restricted entry?
chapters.9.summary: The writer describes the tabernacle: lampstand, table, and the Holy of Holies. Priests entered the outer room daily. Only the high priest entered the inner room, once a year, with blood. The Spirit showed by this that the way in was not yet open. Christ entered the greater tabernacle once, with his own blood. A will takes effect at death, and the first covenant began with blood. Without shedding of blood there is no forgiveness. Christ appeared once to put away sin and will appear again to save.
chapters.10.lds: The selected Church lesson joins meaningful ordinances with continued confidence and trust. Why does confidence before God lead into encouragement of love and good work?
chapters.10.summary: The law has a shadow of good things and repeats the same sacrifices each year. The blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins. Christ came to do God’s will and offered his body once for all. Priests stand daily, but he sat down after one sacrifice. So believers may enter the holy place by the blood of Jesus. They should hold fast their hope and not give up meeting together. The writer warns of judgment for those who sin willfully after knowing the truth. He reminds them how they endured loss with joy.
chapters.11.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches faith as trust in promises not yet fulfilled. Doctrine and Covenants 128:15 applies verse 40 to the living and the dead. Why do victories and painful deaths appear within the same account of faith?
chapters.11.summary: Faith is assurance of things hoped for and proof of things not seen. By faith Abel offered, Enoch pleased God, and Noah built an ark. Abraham left for an unknown land, and Sarah received power to conceive. They died without receiving the promises and looked for a heavenly country. Abraham offered Isaac, and Moses chose mistreatment with God’s people. The walls of Jericho fell, and Rahab was spared. Some conquered kingdoms and escaped the sword. Others were tortured, stoned, sawn apart, and went about destitute.
chapters.12.lds: How do commands to strengthen weak limbs make endurance a shared task?
chapters.12.summary: The writer pictures a race with a great cloud of witnesses around it. The readers should lay aside every weight and run with endurance. They should look to Jesus, who endured the cross. They have not yet resisted to blood. The Lord disciplines those he loves, as a father does his sons. So they should lift tired hands and make straight paths for the lame. They should pursue peace and not sell their birthright as Esau did. They have come to Mount Zion and receive a kingdom that cannot be shaken.
chapters.13.lds: Why does praise join sharing and care for prisoners in the closing directions?
chapters.13.summary: The writer gives closing directions. Let brotherly love continue, and do not forget hospitality to strangers. Remember prisoners as if bound with them. Honor marriage, and be free from the love of money. Remember your leaders, for Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. Jesus suffered outside the gate, so the readers should go out to him. They are to offer praise and to share. The writer asks for prayer, mentions Timothy’s release, and sends greetings from Italy.
